# Sovrium automation triggers and actions

> Generated from the Sovrium schema by scripts/build/generate-skill-references.ts — do not edit. It carries no version on purpose: when it and the binary you run disagree, the binary is right.

Every trigger an automation can start from (9) and every action a step can run (142), in the words of the schema. An action is chosen by its `type` and, within a family, its `operator`.

## Contents

- [Triggers](#triggers)
- [Actions](#actions)

## Triggers

Read: `sovrium docs automation-triggers`

| Type | When it fires |
| --- | --- |
| `webhook` | Trigger automation via incoming HTTP webhook |
| `cron` | Trigger automation on a schedule using cron expressions |
| `record` | Trigger automation when records are created, updated, or deleted. The run reads the row as stored at trigger.data.record (id, created_at, updated_at and the stamped columns included) and, for a record created through the records API or written by an automation step, who made the write at trigger.user ({ id, role, email, name }; id and role read system, email and name empty, for a write no person made). |
| `auth` | Trigger automation on authentication events (sign-up, sign-in, invitation accepted, etc.) |
| `form` | Trigger automation when a top-level form is submitted. The `form` property references forms[].name (HARD BREAK: was a page path). |
| `manual` | Admin-initiated workflow execution via button or API call |
| `automation-call` | Trigger that fires when another automation invokes this one via the automation/call action. Enables sub-workflow composition. |
| `automation-failure` | Trigger an automation when another automation fails. Enables composable failure handling without per-automation notification config. |
| `comment` | Trigger automation when a comment is created on a record. Provides $trigger.comment.*, $trigger.record.*, $trigger.threadParticipants, $trigger.mentions, $trigger.mentionedEmails context variables. |

## Actions

Read: `sovrium docs automation-actions`

| Type | Operator | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `runTypescript` | Execute a named execute(context) function with typed CodeContext including actions and structured logging — body is type-checked at server startup |
| `http` | `get` | Send GET requests to external services — no body field |
| `http` | `post` | Send POST requests to external services — defaults Content-Type to application/json |
| `http` | `put` | Send PUT requests to external services — full resource replacement with JSON default |
| `http` | `patch` | Send PATCH requests to external services — partial resource update with JSON default |
| `http` | `delete` | Send DELETE requests to external services — optional body for APIs that accept it |
| `http` | `request` | Send configurable HTTP requests to external services |
| `record` | `create` | Insert a new record into a table |
| `record` | `read` | Fetch a single record from a table by its primary key |
| `record` | `list` | Read a filtered, ordered, paginated set of records from a table |
| `record` | `update` | Update records matching filter conditions |
| `record` | `delete` | Delete records matching filter conditions |
| `record` | `upsert` | Atomically create a record if not found, or update it if it exists |
| `record` | `batchCreate` | Create multiple records in a single operation |
| `record` | `batchUpdate` | Update multiple records in a single operation |
| `record` | `batchDelete` | Delete multiple records matching a filter condition |
| `record` | `batchUpsert` | Insert or update multiple records using a match field |
| `record` | `aggregate` | Compute count, sum, average, minimum, maximum and percentiles over the records a filter matches, optionally per group, in one database statement; returned as `rows` |
| `filter` | `continue` | Conditionally continue or stop automation based on evaluated conditions |
| `path` | `branch` | Split automation into conditional branches, executed sequentially in declaration order |
| `loop` | `each` | Iterate over an array and execute actions for each item |
| `email` | `send` | Send emails via configured SMTP transport |
| `email` | `suppress` | Stop mailing an address: record a bounce, a complaint or an unsubscribe on the suppression list later bulk sends consult |
| `email` | `stats` | Count the messages a campaign or a category sent, opened, bounced, complained about and unsubscribed from |
| `auth` | `createUser` | Create a new user account |
| `auth` | `assignRole` | Assign a role to an existing user |
| `auth` | `banUser` | Ban a user account |
| `auth` | `unbanUser` | Unban a previously banned user account |
| `auth` | `addToGroup` | Add a user to a declared group; adding an existing member changes nothing |
| `auth` | `removeFromGroup` | Remove a user from a declared group; removing a non-member changes nothing |
| `auth` | `registerOAuthClient` | Register a consent-less, PKCE-only sign-in client for another app, returning its client id and secret |
| `auth` | `rotateOAuthClientSecret` | Replace a sign-in client's secret; the old one stops working at once |
| `auth` | `deleteOAuthClient` | Delete a sign-in client; sign-in through it and its tokens stop working |
| `auth` | `grantAccess` | Give an account access to one record of a scope table under a role; granting it again changes nothing |
| `auth` | `revokeAccess` | Take one record of a scope table away from an account's grants; revoking it again changes nothing |
| `auth` | `listGrantees` | List the accounts granted access to one record of a scope table, as { grantees, count } |
| `auth` | `inviteUser` | Invite a person by email to create their own password and join with a role; reports whether an invitation was sent |
| `analytics` | `track` | Track custom events in the built-in analytics system |
| `link` | `create` | Mint a tracked short link and return its address for a later step to use. Fails the step rather than shadowing a config-declared slug or overwriting one a live link already holds. |
| `link` | `update` | Apply a sparse edit to an existing runtime link. Omitted props are left unchanged; the slug names the target and cannot be renamed. |
| `link` | `delete` | Soft-delete a runtime link so it stops resolving while its click history survives. Fails the step for a config-declared slug. |
| `comment` | `create` | Post a comment on a record's thread, through the same content, reply, mention, moderation and comment-trigger rules as the comments API |
| `comment` | `list` | Read a record's comments, oldest first, as the system or as the triggering user would read them |
| `comment` | `delete` | Soft-delete one comment of a record's thread, as the system or under the triggering user's comment rules |
| `comment` | `update` | Replace the text of one comment of a record's thread, keeping its id, author, date and place, as the system or under the triggering user's edit rule |
| `comment` | `moderate` | Set the moderation status of one comment of a record's thread — approved, pending or rejected — without touching its content, as the system or under the triggering user's moderator permission |
| `notification` | `create` | Notify people of something: one notification per recipient, of a declared kind, listed in the app, sent by email, or kept for a periodic digest that this version does not yet send, as each recipient's preferences for that kind decide |
| `webhook` | `send` | Send outgoing webhook (envelope or pass-through mode) |
| `webhook` | `response` | Construct a custom response for synchronous webhook triggers (respondImmediately: false) |
| `delay` | `wait` | Pause automation execution for a fixed duration or until a specific datetime |
| `delay` | `webhook` | Pause execution until an external webhook callback is received |
| `delay` | `queue` | Process queued automation items one at a time with configurable spacing for rate-limited APIs |
| `automation` | `call` | Invoke another automation as a step. Enables composable workflow architectures. |
| `automation` | `return` | Send output data back to a calling automation. Only effective with automation-call trigger. |
| `connection` | `call` | Call an operation declared on a connection, with typed parameters, authentication, pagination and retry on rate limits handled by Sovrium. |

| `browser` | `agent` | Let an AI agent drive a browser towards a goal on a site with no API, within listed hosts, typing secrets it never sees, its submissions held for approval. Needs the operator to enable a browser (`BROWSER_PROVIDER`) and an AI provider. |

| `file` | `getMetadata` | Read a stored file's metadata without downloading it. The step output carries `key`, `contentType`, `size` (bytes) and `lastModified` (ISO 8601), plus `uploadedBy` (the id of the user who uploaded it, signed in or through an API key) and `generatedBy` (the automation whose document action wrote it), each present only when recorded. A key with no stored file leaves `error` in the output instead. |
